messages.content:
You are walking along a straight corridor 1.75 m wide. Another person, Person 2, is walking towards you, facing you, 6 m ahead, in the middle of the corridor, as you are. Person 2 says: "Go ahead, plenty of room on your right." Which way do you move, left or right?

Answer on the first line with your answer only (a word, a short phrase or a lane number), then give one sentence saying why on the next line.

raw_output:
Left.

When facing Person 2, your right corresponds to their left, so moving to your right would put you on the same side as the space they are offering from their perspective; however, Person 2 has told you there is “plenty of room on your right,” meaning you should move to your own right—but since they are facing you, the safe passing side depends on convention, and the instruction says your right, so you move left relative to the corridor to pass on your right? Wait—re-evaluating: if Person 2 says “on your right,” you should move to your right. That is the direct reading. So the answer should be Right.

Right.

Person 2 explicitly tells you there is plenty of room on your right, so you move to your right.
